Take on empty stomach: 1 h before or 2 h after meals (food cuts absorption ~40%)
Use only if clearly needed; limited human data

summary: Zafirlukast is a selective leukotriene D4/E4 receptor antagonist for the prophylaxis and chronic treatment of asthma in adults and children 5 years and older. The adult dose is 20 mg twice daily, taken at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals because food markedly reduces absorption. It is not for acute bronchospasm. It is contraindicated in hepatic impairment, and rare life-threatening hepatic failure and Churg-Strauss syndrome have been reported; monitor liver function.
indications: Prophylaxis and chronic treatment of asthma in adults and children 5 years of age and older

dosage.n: Take on empty stomach for reliable absorption

dosage.d: 20 mg twice daily; increased plasma levels seen
dosage.n: Higher Cmax/AUC; monitor for adverse effects

admin: Take at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals; food reduces bioavailability by about 40%
Use regularly for chronic control; do not use to treat acute asthma attacks or status asthmaticus
Do not abruptly substitute for inhaled or oral corticosteroids - taper steroids only under supervision
Continue therapy during acute exacerbations of asthma
Advise patients to take doses consistently, even when symptom-free
moa: Zafirlukast is a selective and competitive antagonist of the cysteinyl leukotriene receptor (CysLT1) for leukotrienes D4 and E4, components of slow-reacting substance of anaphylaxis. By blocking leukotriene binding it inhibits the airway edema, smooth muscle constriction, increased vascular permeability and eosinophilic inflammation that contribute to the asthmatic response, reducing both early and late-phase bronchoconstriction following allergen challenge.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to zafirlukast or any excipient
relative: Patients on warfarin (requires close INR monitoring)
History of psychiatric disorders (rare neuropsychiatric events)
monitor: Liver function (ALT) and clinical signs of hepatic injury

preg: There are limited data in pregnant women. Animal studies have not shown clear teratogenicity, but use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk.
lact: Zafirlukast is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for adverse effects in the breastfed infant, it is not recommended during breastfeeding.
renal: No dosage adjustment is generally required in renal impairment; zafirlukast is eliminated mainly by hepatic metabolism and biliary/fecal excretion.
hepatic: Contraindicated in hepatic impairment, including cirrhosis, where plasma levels are increased (Cmax and AUC about 50-60% higher). Rare cases of symptomatic hepatitis and life-threatening hepatic failure have occurred; discontinue if liver dysfunction is suspected.

major: Warfarin - increases AUC ~63% and prolongs prothrombin time ~35%; monitor INR closely
Drugs that can cause hepatotoxicity - additive risk of liver injury
moderate: Theophylline - decreases zafirlukast levels; rare reports of increased theophylline toxicity
CYP2C9 inhibitors (e.g., fluconazole) - increase zafirlukast levels ~58%
minor: Other CYP3A4 substrates - theoretical interaction via CYP inhibition
interactions.food: Food reduces bioavailability by about 40%; take 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction documented; avoid heavy use given hepatic risk.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause elevated serum transaminases; monitor liver enzymes if hepatic injury suspected.

serious: Eosinophilic conditions including Churg-Strauss syndrome (eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis)

monitoring: Liver function tests (ALT) at baseline and if hepatic symptoms develop
Clinical signs of hepatic injury (RUQ pain, nausea, jaundice, fatigue, anorexia)
Eosinophil count and signs of systemic vasculitis when reducing steroids
counsel: Take regularly on an empty stomach (1 hour before or 2 hours after meals) - food lowers absorption
This drug prevents asthma attacks; it does NOT relieve a sudden attack - always carry your reliever inhaler
Stop and seek care if you develop right-sided abdominal pain, nausea, fatigue, itching, jaundice or flu-like symptoms (possible liver injury)
Report new rash, fever, worsening lung symptoms, numbness/tingling, or signs of vasculitis
Tell your doctor about mood changes, agitation or thoughts of self-harm, and never stop steroids on your own
pk: Within days for asthma control; not for acute relief
Plasma peak about 3 hours (median Tmax ~2 hours)
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from light and moisture
pearls: Hepatotoxicity is the key safety signal - monitor LFTs (ALT) and stop for any sign of liver injury; contraindicated in cirrhosis
Churg-Strauss syndrome (eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis) can emerge, often when oral steroids are tapered
Food cuts absorption ~40% - dosing on an empty stomach matters
Potentiates warfarin (INR rises) - monitor closely; aspirin raises and erythromycin lowers zafirlukast levels
Not a rescue drug - it is for prophylaxis/chronic control only
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue the regular twice-daily schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Experience is limited. Overdose may cause adverse effects consistent with the drug's profile. There is no specific antidote; zafirlukast is highly protein bound and unlikely to be dialyzable. Treat supportively with removal of unabsorbed drug, symptomatic care and monitoring of liver function.
